A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research lineage, with the same authors and shared prototype/hypergradient framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions and retitling.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-learning experiments on CIFAR100, CUB, and ImageNet-R, including benchmark results, component ablations, sensitivity studies, and execution times.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark comparisons, VTAB-based hyperparameter experiments, component ablations, gradient analyses, and appendix measurements of accuracy and computational resources.

M1.justification: v1's CWH learns one coefficient per class and rescales final-layer gradients. v2 Section 3.3 and Algorithm 1 specify elementwise coefficients for every trainable parameter, including parameters outside the classification head. This changes the procedure beyond renaming CWH to FGH. The online prototype update and additive prototype loss are retained, although v2's implementation appendix conflicts with its revised method.

E1.justification: CIFAR100, CUB, and ImageNet-R remain the principal evaluation datasets, with clear and Si-Blurry boundaries. v2 adds VTAB for auxiliary hyperparameter selection and gamma sensitivity experiments (Section 4.1, Figure 3, and Appendix A.6), providing a limited extension of dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v2 retains L2P, DualPrompt, CODA, ConvPrompt, and MVP, while adding evaluated comparisons with oLoRA, full fine-tuning, linear probing, Experience Replay, and Experience Replay with linear probing. These additions substantially broaden the comparator set in both clear and Si-Blurry experiments (Tables 1–2).

E3.justification: The main benchmark batch size changes from 10 to 100. v1 evaluates three fixed learning rates and their average; v2 uses two fixed rates plus settings selected on VTAB. The stated default gamma changes from 0.001 to 1. v2 also introduces gradient-norm diagnostics, revises the gamma sweep, and replaces aggregate old-class reporting with individual-task results in the clear setting.

E4.justification: v1 already tests hypergradients without prototypes for CODA on CUB (Table 6); v2 expands this component comparison to four prompt methods and three datasets (Table 3). It adds gradient-imbalance and gradient-trajectory analyses (Figures 1–2 and A6–A35) and detailed retention analyses. The final-layer learning-rate multiplier, frozen-backbone/prototype-drift, and coefficient-evolution studies in v1 are removed, while gamma sensitivity is substantially revised.

E5.justification: Reported replication increases from three seeds in v1's main experiments to ten for most methods in v2; ConvPrompt and oLoRA use three. v1's separate CODA ablation used five runs. Both versions retain mean and standard-deviation reporting and seed-dependent task generation, without introducing confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Most benchmark results are replaced, with additional comparator, gradient, memory-footprint, and task-specific results. For example, clear-setting CIFAR100 AP at learning rate 0.005 is 78.16±1.43 for L2P+OP+CWH in v1 Table 2 and 82.26±0.76 for L2P+prototypes+FGH in v2 Table 2. These use different methods and batch sizes, so they do not establish a same-setting improvement. Results for MVP augmented with the proposed components are removed.

T1.justification: v2 adapts the hypergradient derivation from class-specific final-layer vectors to individual trainable parameters and introduces formal definitions of averaged class/task gradient norms and their normalization (Section 5.1, Equation 10). The underlying chain-rule argument and prototype mathematics remain substantially the same; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes prototypes and class-wise hypergradients for missing task boundaries and unknown learning rates. v2 makes memory-free, task-free offline-to-online adaptation and prototype-induced gradient imbalance central contributions. It claims that all-parameter FGH addresses this imbalance and that the combined approach surpasses online memory-free baselines and competes with replay, substantially redirecting the paper's claims.

C2.justification: v1 explains improvements through stable pretrained representations and class-dependent learning-rate behavior. v2 instead develops a mechanism involving prototype-amplified gradient imbalance, its reversal by FGH, and continued updates supporting older tasks. It explains performance drops without prototypes through reduced stability, adds qualifications about large-gamma instability and oLoRA's setting sensitivity, and removes the prototype-drift discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds implementation-source references, the timm model identifier, VTAB search grids and selected settings, replay storage/retrieval details, and GPU-memory measurements. However, Appendix A.2 identifies Algorithm 2 as the experimental implementation while that algorithm retains v1's class-wise final-layer update and gamma=0.001, conflicting with the main text's all-parameter FGH and default gamma=1. The authors' own code remains promised upon acceptance in both versions.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around memory-based versus memory-free continual learning, replacing the earlier PTM-centered related-work subsection with a memory-buffer discussion. Added references include Continual Prototype Evolution, Online Prototype Learning, Online-LoRA, and Hyperparameters in Continual Learning: A Reality Check. These additions contextualize the prototype and hyperparameter contributions beyond a bibliographic refresh.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Method presentation is reorganized around online adaptation, prototypes, and FGH; the former standalone learning-rate discussion is compressed or moved to the appendix. Discussion sections and appendix organization are also substantially reworked.

P2.justification: v2 switches from two-column to single-column layout, restructures comparison tables around new baseline groups and Best HP columns, and adds extensive gradient plots and task-specific tables. Prototype-drift and coefficient plots disappear. v1 Figures 1 and 5 are retained as Figures A4 and A5; A4 also corrects the low-learning-rate legend. These are substantial display changes beyond pagination.

improvement.justification: Broader baselines, VTAB-transfer evaluation, increased replication, and component/gradient analyses strengthen the evidence. However, v2's claimed all-parameter FGH conflicts with Algorithm 2, explicitly identified as the implementation used, leaving the evaluated procedure uncertain. Its claim of matching or exceeding replay at every tested learning rate also conflicts with Table 1: at 0.00005 on CIFAR100, ER achieves 81.33% versus at most 44.23% for the augmented methods. These substantive consistency problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the additions.
